references.text: Jesus had previously commanded the disciples not to tell anyone that he was the Christ, and predicted his suffering. The disciples' silence after the transfiguration on the mountain corresponds with this command to keep it secret.
Matthew's parallel account of the transfiguration on the mountain, where Jesus also commands the disciples not to tell anyone about the vision until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.
Mark's parallel account of the transfiguration on the mountain, where the disciples kept this to themselves and discussed what rising from the dead meant.

The verse just before, where a cloud came over them and a voice sounded from the cloud. Luke 9:36 tells what happened after the voice had sounded – Jesus was found alone, and Moses and Elijah were gone.
In Matthew's account, the disciples lift their eyes and see no one else but Jesus alone, which corresponds to Luke's description that Jesus was found alone after the voice had sounded.
Mark describes the same moment: suddenly they looked around and saw no one else but Jesus alone with them, and he forbade them to tell anyone about what they had seen.

Peter later refers back to the transfiguration on the mountain as an eyewitness, confirming that they saw Jesus' glory and heard the voice from heaven – even though they originally kept silent about the experience.
